temples.name: Chennakeshava
temples.introduction: An encounter with the rhythm of Hoysala stonework. Explore a representative pillared hall, a stellate platform and ornamental bands inspired by the temple at Belur.

elements.name: Lathe-turned pillar
elements.description: Circular mouldings and polished shafts distinguish many Hoysala columns. This simplified study makes the changing profile visible from every angle.

elements.name: Stellate platform
elements.description: Projecting and receding edges create a rhythmic footprint. The raised platform provides a route around the shrine. This model abstracts the plan rather than reproducing a survey.

elements.name: Ornamental frieze
elements.description: Stacked carved bands articulate Hoysala exteriors. Repeated geometric motifs stand in for the much more intricate carvings of the real monument.

timeline.title: A Hoysala foundation
timeline.description: Chennakeshava at Belur dates to 1117 CE, during the reign of Vishnuvardhana.

timeline.title: An evolving tradition
timeline.description: Hoysala workshops developed richly articulated plans, polished columns and elaborate stone ornament.

timeline.title: World Heritage
timeline.description: Belur and Halebidu are components of the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas, inscribed by UNESCO in 2023.

timeline.title: A living temple
timeline.description: Worship continues at Belur. This digital study represents selected architectural ideas, not the full complex.

temples.name: Hoysaleswara
temples.introduction: Two shrine forms, a shared platform and an extraordinary sculptural tradition. This section studies Halebidu through its paired composition and richly layered exterior.

elements.name: Moulded pillar
elements.description: Alternating discs, necks and capitals give the column its measured silhouette. Rotate this study to examine the relationship between a profile and a surface of revolution.

elements.name: Paired shrine study
elements.description: Hoysaleswara is known for its paired sanctuaries. These low, stepped masses are a schematic study of that relationship, not a reconstruction of lost roof forms.

elements.name: Relief register
elements.description: Horizontal registers organize the richly carved exterior. Abstract repeating motifs communicate their rhythm without claiming to reproduce specific sacred figures.

timeline.title: The Hoysala capital
timeline.description: The Hoysaleswara complex developed at Halebidu during the Hoysala period.

timeline.title: Stone as narrative
timeline.description: Sculptural registers and carefully articulated architecture became hallmarks of the Hoysala tradition.

timeline.title: World Heritage
timeline.description: Halebidu joined Belur and Somanathapura in the UNESCO-listed Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas.

timeline.title: Conservation and study
timeline.description: The surviving architecture supports continued research and conservation. This model is an educational abstraction.

temples.name: Virupaksha
temples.introduction: A monumental gateway rises above a landscape of granite. Explore an interpretation of Virupaksha's entrance tower and the ordered columns of a temple courtyard.

elements.name: Mandapa column
elements.description: Stone columns organize covered gathering spaces. This geometric column study emphasizes the base, shaft, capital and the beam it supports.

elements.name: Gopuram study
elements.description: A gopuram marks a temple entrance with a tapering, tiered silhouette. This scaled study abstracts the tower's massing and repeated architectural details.

elements.name: Pavilion cornice
elements.description: Projecting roof edges cast a clear shadow over a pavilion. Repetition ties individual supports into a continuous architectural space.

timeline.title: A sacred site
timeline.description: Virupaksha's sacred history predates the Vijayanagara capital. Its buildings reflect multiple phases.

timeline.title: Vijayanagara
timeline.description: Hampi flourished as the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire. Monumental religious architecture shaped its landscape.

timeline.title: World Heritage
timeline.description: The Group of Monuments at Hampi was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1986.

timeline.title: A living sacred place
timeline.description: Virupaksha remains a place of worship. Its continued use has brought changes and additions across time.
